title: Whitelist Do's and Don'ts
description: Whitelisting, learn what we are looking for as part of the whitelist process.
content:
**How to Whitelist Your Character**

This guide is meant to help you understand what kinds of information are important in a whitelist application, how to present it clearly, and what is generally acceptable within the setting. Think of this less as a list of questions and more as a set of guidelines to help you tell us who your character is and why they matter.

A strong whitelist focuses on the parts of your character that actively shape how they act, think, and interact in the world right now. Not every detail of a life story needs to be included. What matters most are the things that push your character forward.

**What to Focus On**

Explain any magical, alchemical, technological, or scientific interests your character has had. These should be framed as studies, experiments, research interests, partial successes, or outright failures. Fully finished, mass-producible, or easily deployable inventions are not appropriate at character start.

If your character has access to special devices, techniques, or unusual magic, keep them mostly flavor-based. Knowing of something or having assisted with advanced work does not mean your character fully understands or can recreate it.

Be clear and realistic about your character’s level of expertise. If they worked in a controlled institution, such as a Nexarcan laboratory or similar organization, explain what they realistically would have been allowed to see or work on. Most people only ever understand a small piece of a much larger system.

Highlight pivotal moments in your character’s life. These can be traumatic events, major failures, personal losses, or defining successes. These moments should help explain who your character is today and how they react to the world around them.

Describe the personality traits that truly define your character. Focus on traits that will meaningfully show up in roleplay, such as ambition, loyalty, pride, insecurity, anger, curiosity, or compassion.

Explain why your character has come to Vardoran. What pushed them away from their previous life? What pulled them here? What do they want, and what keeps them moving forward?

If your character has grand goals, especially magical, scientific, or world-altering ones, explain how they intend to pursue them. The larger the ambition, the more detail we need to understand the path you plan to take.

**What to Avoid**

Avoid writing extensive family trees, childhood anecdotes, or romantic histories unless they are directly relevant to your character’s current motivations. Distant relatives, old crushes, or one-off childhood events usually do not meaningfully affect present roleplay.

Do not write direct connections to existing in-game characters such as Dracula or other VBloods. Your character should stand on their own rather than being pre-attached to major canon figures.

Do not write your character as all-powerful, invincible, or universally exceptional. Characters who are geniuses, master warriors, or flawless problem-solvers need to be supported by both setting logic and player capability.

If you want your character to be skilled but you are still learning the game mechanically, consider starting them as inexperienced, aspiring, or early in their journey. Growth through roleplay is always more satisfying than starting at the top.

Do not copy existing characters wholesale. Inspiration is encouraged, but take a single idea or theme you enjoy and build something original around it.

Avoid trying to make your character untouchable. Weaknesses, flaws, vices, and emotional soft spots create better roleplay opportunities. Pride, fear, addiction, guilt, or misplaced loyalty all give other characters ways to meaningfully engage with yours.

**Technology and Advancement**

Do not assume technology progressed the same way it did in the real world. Magic fundamentally altered the development of science in this setting. Two hundred years in Vardoran does not equal two hundred years of real-world technological advancement.

Technological stagnation, regression, or strange divergence is expected. If you want to pursue advanced creations, consider how magic supplements or replaces real-world technology rather than mimicking it exactly.

Anything truly advanced must be earned through roleplay, effort, setbacks, and staff oversight. Starting with partial knowledge and growing over time is the intended experience.

**Final Notes**

This guide is not meant to limit creativity, but to keep the setting grounded, collaborative, and fun for everyone involved. If you are ever unsure whether something fits, ask. We are always happy to help you shape an idea into something that works within the world.
